messages:
Sam L: Hey team — onboarding note for Kestrel-7B (vendor X). License includes an NC clause + an export-control sentence referencing a vendor-managed embargo list. Also says 'derivative weights allowed with attribution and upstream notice'.
Anya R: Do we have precedent for NC + hosting? Sounds like Hosted API (paid customers) might violate NC if used commercially.
LegalBot: Flag: Potential incompatibility with hosted and dedicated offerings. NC (non-commercial) typically prohibits commercial exploitation. Need product/legal review.
Mike T: On the technical side, we plan to quantize to 4-bit for latency. Vendor rep verbally said 'quantization permitted' but the license text is ambiguous about distribution of quantized binaries or container images.
Sam L: Quoted from license: "You may create derivative works (including quantized variants) provided attribution is included and redistribution is limited to 'internal project distribution' unless prior written consent obtained." — that reads restrictive.
Julia C: For Dedicated customers we don't publish weights, but for Private we currently provide a deployment package (container) that includes optimized kernels + weights. That might fall under redistribution.
Anya R: @LegalBot can you confirm whether shipping a container to a paying customer counts as redistribution under that clause?
LegalBot: Quick read: 'redistribution' likely includes transferring a binary/container to third parties. If redistribution is limited to 'internal' we'd need written consent for shipping to customers. Recommend we request an explicit exception for 'customer deployment packages' from the vendor.
Mike T: Related question: if we keep weights on our side and only expose inference via API (hosted), does NC still block that? My interpretation: providing paid API access using the model is commercial exploitation and probably violates NC.
Sam L: Also note vendor's export-control line: "Model weights are not authorized for export to certain jurisdictions per vendor policy." Ops/infra will need to ensure region gating and not serve inference from disallowed regions.
Julia C: For Private on-prem where the customer pulls the package from their own VPC, we might avoid us shipping containers. But the license still requires attribution in product docs; we need a standard attribution snippet.
Anya R: On evals: after quantizing to 4-bit we saw a small but consistent quality regression on our convo benchmark (rounds-based). We should capture that in the eval and include it in vendor questions: ask whether vendor would permit higher-precision builds for customer distributions or provide a sanctioned quantized build.
Mike T: Sharing quick eval numbers: ```diff
- baseline fp16 perplexity: 12.8
- 4-bit (QLoRA): 13.6
+ relative delta: +6.25%
``` small but consistent across intents. Latency improved ~35%.
Sam L: Action items: 1) Legal to request written redistribution carve-out for customer deployment containers and clarify export whitelist. 2) Vendor: request explicit permission for quantized releases and an approved attribution text. 3) Eng to run full A/B regressions and prepare attribution snippet and deployment checklist. I'll draft PRD.
LegalBot: Created ticket LEG-492: vendor carve-out request + export control clarification.
Anya R: I'll attach eval artifacts, license scan PDF, and the quoted license snippet to LEG-492.
Julia C: Ops note: blocked on vendor clarifying export list before we enable Dedicated regions in eu-west-2 and ap-southeast-1 for this model.
Mike T: I'll run the full eval suite and bench 4-bit vs fp16 throughput/cost for the PRD.
Sam L: Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
LegalBot: Reminder: do not ship containers or enable customer-facing deployments for Kestrel-7B until vendor sign-off is in LEG-492.
